name: Total Cost Input for WooCommerce
author: ethereumicoio

sections.description:
Total Cost Input for WooCommerce plugin lets customers enter the amount of money they want to spend. The matching product quantity is calculated for them and shown right next to the sum (and, in the PRO version, the customer can also type the quantity and the two numbers stay in sync).

This plugin is ideal to sell products that can not be counted in portions, like liquids, powders, gas, cryptocurrencies, etc.

With this plugin used, your customer can just enter a sum, like $100 for example, and buy some amount of product you are selling, in grams, litres, bitcoins, etc.

It can be a valuable addition to your crypto selling store with the Cryptocurrency WordPress Plugin for WooCommerce!

Features

  • Your customer types the sum, not the quantity: on a product that sells by the total, entering $9.9 at a $100 unit price shows 0.099 units next to the amount, and that is the quantity that goes into the cart.
  • The sum field is switched on per product: one checkbox on the product’s General tab makes that product, and only that product, ask for a total instead of a quantity.
  • One settings screen controls the sale: the quantity step (0.001, 0.1, …), the order of the widget fields, each field’s width out of twelve columns, the button text and the widget style.
  • Sell by the sum from any page: the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode, or the Total Cost Input block in the editor, shows the product, the sum and the resulting quantity in a finished Material card.
  • The widget’s dropdown lists the products by name only, with no prices in the list, so the buyer picks the coin rather than comparing numbers.
  • The field order is yours: the sum can come first and the product after the quantity, set per shortcode, per block or once for the whole site.
  • The card is arranged in the block editor, not in code: the inspector reorders the four fields, sets each field’s width out of twelve columns, and the Professional version adds a Style panel with the style mode, colours, font, size and corner radii.
  • All four fields – the sum, the quantity, the product and Buy – sit side by side on one line: each field takes a span of 1 to 12 columns, and 4 + 4 + 1 + 3 fills a row of twelve exactly, with no separate layout switch.

PRO Features

  • On the product page the two fields stay in sync in either direction: type 0.05 units and the sum becomes $5.00.
  • The widget’s quantity field is editable too, so the buyer types the units instead of only reading the number the sum produced.
  • A custom style paints the widget: the card and button colours, the text colour, the font family and size, and the corner radii of the card and of the button.
  • The custom style works in a one-row layout as well: the same colours, font and radii with the fields sharing the line.

Works with

  • Classic WooCommerce product, cart and checkout templates, on WooCommerce 5.5 and newer.
  • In the Professional version the widget can offer the products of the current vendor only, on a WC Vendors, Dokan or WCFM page. No screenshot confirms this one: it is a per-page restriction with no screen of its own.
  • In the Professional version the widget’s product list can be restricted to the products you choose. No screenshot confirms this one either, for the same reason.
  • The widget’s product list holds the shop’s sellable set only: published products, in stock or on backorder, and simple enough to price per unit. No screenshot confirms this one either: the list shows two names and carries no stock or visibility marker.
  • In the Professional version the buy button carries your text instead of Buy, and the widget can take the look of the site theme; both are rows on the settings screen shown above.

Not supported yet

Block-based product surfaces are not supported yet. The Total Cost Input field works on the classic single-product template and on the classic cart and checkout. The block versions of those pages (the Single Product block, the Cart and Checkout blocks) render the quantity field on the client side and therefore ignore the plugin’s field:

  • Single Product block – no Total Cost Input field;
  • Cart and Checkout blocks – no money/quantity synchronisation.

Use the classic templates (or the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode / block, which is unaffected) until a future release adds the block support.

sections.installation:
• Install and activate it as you would any other plugin.
  • Make a new WooCommerce product, or just check the Total Cost Input checkbox on an existing one.
  • To sell from a widget, drop the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode, or the total-cost-input-for-woocommerce/widget block (titled Total Cost Input in the inserter list), into a page.
sections.changelog:
2.1.0

  • Requires PHP 8.1: the PHP floor moved from 7.4 to 8.1 (2026-11-13), so the supported combination is WordPress 6.6 or newer with PHP 8.1 or newer. On an older PHP the plugin refuses to load and shows an admin notice instead of failing on the first 8.1-only line.
  • The extension points the 2.x contract stamps 2.1.0 are listed here for the first time, with their signatures in docs/contracts/filters-hooks.md: the filters total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_config, total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_amount, total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_redirect_url, total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_catalog_query_args, total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_catalog_products, total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_catalog_label and total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_catalog_visibilities, and the actions total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_before_select, total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_after_select and total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_empty.
  • The 2.1.0 upgrade step, total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_upgrade_2_1_0, writes the documented Buy default into the existing option when the site has no button-text key yet. A text you already chose – including an empty one – is left alone.

2.0.0

  • Rewritten on a layered architecture: app/ is split into Domain / Views / Controllers / Modules, and Infrastructure\Hooks is the only place that registers a hook. The plugin option, the product meta key, the public hooks and the total_cost asset handle are unchanged, so an upgrade keeps the configuration.
  • The Total Cost Input per-product checkbox is now part of the FREE version.
  • The Product Quantity Step setting is FREE too: enter 0.1 and the customer can buy 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 … without a licence.
  • The global/quantity-input.php template override was rebased on WooCommerce 10.1.0 (unified woocommerce_before/after_quantity_input_field hooks, aria-label, conditional size / max).
  • The PRO-only “show the quantity field too” option no longer hides the field with CSS: the standard quantity input is a hidden field and the visible one is rendered by PRO only.
  • New product-sale widget: the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode and the Total Cost Input: Product Gutenberg block – a dropdown of every product that can be bought right now (names only, no prices) and a Buy button that adds the product to the cart and takes the customer straight to the checkout.
  • PRO: the widget’s amount field (a sum in the site currency), the product-list restriction, a custom button text, a theme style (the widget inherits the site theme’s own styling), a custom style (widget and button background, text colour, font family and size, corner radius) and the vendor restriction on WC Vendors / Dokan / WCFM pages.
  • The widget is a flat 12-column grid: every field claims a span of 1 to 12 columns and a field that spans all twelve takes the whole row, so the card stacks by default and smaller spans make a row. The old layout attribute/option (vertical/horizontal) is gone – the spans are the layout.
  • The front end is a Vite + React bundle. jQuery is no longer used – not a dependency, not in the code – and assets/widget.js and the root *.js / *.min.js files are gone.
  • A widget that renders nothing publishes the reason (empty_catalog, no_vendor, no_vendor_products) through total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_empty.
  • The products attribute of the widget is cast with (int), so a negative id means “no products” rather than product 1.
  • Requires WordPress 6.6 and PHP 7.4; tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2.
  • Known limitation: block-based product surfaces (the Single Product block, the Cart and Checkout blocks) are not supported yet.

1.1.3

  • freemius library version update
  • tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2

1.1.2

  • freemius library version update

1.1.1

  • freemius library version update

1.1.0

  • The Product Quantity Step setting is introduced. Enter 0.1 to allow customer to buy 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, e.t.c. quantity of your products.

1.0.2

  • WooCommerce global/quantity-input.php template update to the latest version

1.0.1

  • freemius library version update

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
